This adds a mode where the vcore scheduling logic in HV KVM limits itself
to scheduling only virtual cores from the same VM on any given physical
core.  This is enabled via a new module parameter on the kvm-hv module
called ""one_vm_per_core"".  For this to work on POWER9
set indep_threads_mode=N.  (On POWER8
is never in independent threads mode
setting.)
Thus the settings needed for this to work are:
1. The host is in SMT1 mode.
2. On POWER8
column2: the host is not in 2-way or 4-way static split-core mode.

column1: 3. On POWER9
4. The one_vm_per_core parameter is Y.
With these settings
column2: KVM can run up to 4 vcpus on a core at the same

column1: time on POWER9
column2: or up to 8 vcpus on POWER8 (depending on the guest

column1: threading mode)
column2: and will ensure that all of the vcpus belong to the

column1: same VM.
This is intended for use in security-conscious settings where users are
concerned about possible side-channel attacks between threads which could
perhaps enable one VM to attack another VM on the same core
